description: Threat Hunting (app/services/threat_hunting) inputs. A hunt is created as a draft and then run exactly once by the real ThreatHuntService against real persisted data (detections, correlations, risk assessments, TI indicators/lookups, incident memories, audit log). No finding, evidence item or timeline entry is written here - all of them are produced by the hunting engine. Filters are constrained by HUNT_TYPE_FIELDS and FIELD_OPERATORS in app/schemas/threat_hunting.py; an unsupported field/operator pair is rejected at validation, never silently ignored.

window.note: Hours relative to now at run time; resolved by the runner to timezone-aware instants.

hunts.name: DEMO: detection review of the full SOC chain
hunts.purpose: Reviews the persisted detections produced by the 00_full_soc_scenario ingest and reports them as governed evidence + findings.

hunts.name: DEMO: indicator hunt for the delivery host
hunts.purpose: Looks up a real persisted threat-intel indicator and its provider lookups.

hunts.name: DEMO: multi-stage activity for the full SOC correlation
hunts.purpose: Reads the persisted correlation, its members and the correlated risk assessment for the scenario correlation id.

hunts.name: DEMO: privilege activity review
hunts.purpose: Second detection-surface template, adding the risk_level field, to show the filter/field allowlist differs per hunt type.

lifecycle.note: ThreatHuntService.run -> status=completed; single-shot, a completed hunt cannot be re-run
list_evidence / list_findings / list_timeline -> deterministic paged read models
ThreatHuntService.cancel on a non-terminal draft -> status=cancelled, audited
